In [[probability theory]], '''Lévy's stochastic area''' is a [[stochastic process]] that describes the enclosed area of a [[trajectory]] of a two-dimensional [[Brownian motion]] and its [[Chord (geometry)|chord]]. The process was introduced by [[Paul Lévy (mathematician)|Paul Lévy]] in 1940,<ref>{{cite journal|first=Paul M.|last=Lévy|title=Le Mouvement Brownien Plan|journal=American Journal of Mathematics|volume=62|number=1|date=1940|pages=487–550|doi=10.2307/2371467|jstor=2371467 }}</ref> and in 1950<ref name="Levy">{{cite journal|first=Paul M.|last=Lévy|title=Wiener's random function, and other Laplacian random functions|journal=Proc. 2nd Berkeley Symp. Math. Stat. Proba.|volume=II|pages=171–186|publisher=Univ. California|date=1950}}</ref> he computed the [[Characteristic function (probability theory)|characteristic function]] and conditional characteristic function.

The process has many unexpected connections to other objects in mathematics such as the [[soliton]] solutions of the [[Korteweg–De Vries equation]]<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Nobuyuki|last1=Ikeda|first2=Setsuo|last2=Taniguchi|title=The Itô–Nisio theorem, quadratic Wiener functionals, and 1-solitons|journal=Stoch. Proc. Appl.|volume=120|date=2010|issue=5 |pages=605–621|doi=10.1016/j.spa.2010.01.009 |doi-access=free}}</ref> and the [[Riemann zeta function]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Philippe|last1=Biane|first2=Jim|last2=Pitman|first3=Marc|last3=Yor|title=Probability laws related to the Jacobi theta and Riemann zeta functions, and Brownian excursions|journal=Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. (N.S.)|volume=38|date=2001|number=4|pages=435–465|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-01-00912-0 |s2cid=14710582 |doi-access=free}}</ref> In the [[Malliavin calculus]], the process can be used to construct a process that is [[smooth function|smooth]] in the sense of Malliavin but that has no [[continuous function|continuous]] modification with respect to the [[Banach space|Banach norm]].<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Nobuyuki|last1=Ikeda|first2=Shinzō|last2=Watanabe|publisher=Elsevier|title=An Introduction to Malliavin's Calculus|journal=North-Holland Mathematical Library|volume=32|date=1984|isbn=0-444-87588-3|pages=1–52|doi=10.1016/S0924-6509(08)70387-8}}</ref>

==Lévy's stochastic area==
Let <math>W=(W_s^{(1)},W_s^{(2)})_{s\geq 0}</math> be a two-dimensional Brownian motion in <math>\mathbb{R}^2</math> then '''Lévy's stochastic area''' is the process
:<math>S(t,W)=\frac{1}{2}\int_0^t \left(W_s^{(1)}dW_s^{(2)}-W_s^{(2)}dW_s^{(1)}\right),</math>
where the [[Itō integral]] is used.<ref name="Levy" />

Define the [[Differential form|1-Form]] <math>\vartheta=\tfrac{1}{2}(x^1dx^2-x^2dx^1)</math> then <math>S(t,W)</math> is the stochastic integral of <math>\vartheta</math> along the curve <math>\varphi:[0,t]\to \R^2, s\mapsto (W_s^{(1)},W_s^{(2)})</math>
:<math>S(t,W)=\int_{W[0,t]} \vartheta.</math><ref>{{cite journal|first1=Nobuyuki|last1=Ikeda|first2=Setsuo|last2=Taniguchi|title=Euler polynomials, Bernoulli polynomials, and Lévyʼs stochastic area formula|journal=Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques| volume=135|number=6–7|date=2011 |page=685 |doi=10.1016/j.bulsci.2011.07.009|doi-access=free}}</ref>

===Area formula===
Let <math>x=(x_1,x_2)\in \R^2</math>, <math>a\in \R</math>, <math>b=at/2</math> and <math>S_t=S(t,W)</math> then Lévy computed
:<math>\mathbb{E}[\exp(iaS_t)]=\frac{1}{\cosh(b)}</math>
and
:<math>\mathbb{E}[\exp(iaS_t)\mid W_t=x]=\frac{b}{\sinh(b)}\exp\left(\frac{\|x\|_2}{2t}\left(1-b\coth\left(b\right)\right)\right),</math>
where <math>\|x\|_2</math> is the [[Euclidean norm]].<ref name="Levy"/>{{rp|172–173}}

==Further topics==
* In 1980 [[Marc Yor|Yor]] found a short probabilistic proof.<ref>{{cite conference|first=Marc |last=Yor|date=1980|title=Remarques sur une formule de paul levy|editor-first1=J.|editor-last1=Azéma|editor-first2=M.|editor-last2=Yor|conference=Séminaire de Probabilités XIV 1978/79.|series=Lecture Notes in Mathematics|volume=784|publisher=Springer|place=Berlin, Heidelberg|doi=10.1007/BFb0089501|url=http://www.numdam.org/item/SPS_1980__14__343_0.pdf}}</ref>
* In 1983 Helmes and Schwane found a higher-dimensional formula.<ref>{{cite journal|first1=Kurt|last1=Helmes|first2=A|last2=Schwane|title=Levy's stochastic area formula in higher dimensions|journal=Journal of Functional Analysis|volume=54|number=2|date=1983|pages=177–192|doi=10.1016/0022-1236(83)90053-8}}
</ref>
